answer: Reciprocal Edge Pulse: each node periodically pings a random sample of its neighbors, and edges that fail to return a timely pulse decay. To forge sustained presence, an attacker must keep every fake node answering sampled pulses from real neighbors, which requires live infrastructure per identity, not just a keypair. Honest nodes naturally form a dense haven of mutual pulses, while isolated clusters stand out and get deprioritized in routing. An attacker's cost scales with concurrent responsiveness per fake identity, not one-time registration.
